subject: math
title: Telling Time to the Hour and Half Hour
seo_title: Grade 1 Telling Time Worksheets: Hour and Half Hour (O'Clock and Half Past)
standard_text: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 telling time worksheets with clock pictures: o'clock and half past, matching clocks with hands to digital clocks, where the hands point, and times in daily life. 100 practice questions with an answer key for 1st grade.
key_big: Long hand on the 12 = o'clock (:00). Long hand on the 6 = half past (:30).
key_sub: The short hand tells the hour. At half past it is halfway between two numbers: use the number it has passed, so half past 3 is 3:30, not 4:30.
body_html:
The big idea

A clock has two hands. The short hand is the hour hand. The long hand is the minute hand. Look at the short hand first. Then look at the long hand.

  1. Long hand on the 12: it is an o'clock time. Write :00.
  2. Long hand on the 6: it is half past. Write :30.
  3. Short hand: it tells the hour. If it is between two numbers, use the number it has passed.

Half past

Half past means 30 minutes after the hour. The long hand has gone half of the way around. The short hand has moved halfway to the next number.

WordsDigitalLong handShort hand
3 o'clock3:00on the 12on the 3
half past 33:30on the 6between 3 and 4
4 o'clock4:00on the 12on the 4
Example 1

The short hand is on the 9. The long hand is on the 12. What time is it?

The long hand on the 12 means o'clock. The short hand tells the hour: 9.

Answer: 9:00, 9 o'clock

Example 2

The short hand is between 6 and 7. The long hand is on the 6. What time is it?

The long hand on the 6 means half past. The short hand has passed the 6, so the hour is 6.

Answer: 6:30, half past 6

Example 3

It is 4:30. What time will it be in half an hour?

The long hand moves from the 6 up to the 12. A new hour starts.

Answer: 5:00

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading half past 3 as 4:30 because the short hand is near the 4Use the number the short hand has passed: 3:30
Switching the hands (reading 6:00 as 12:30)Short hand = hour. Long hand = minutes
Writing half past 3 as 3:03 or 30:3Hour first, then a colon, then 30: 3:30
Reading the long hand on the 6 as 6 minutesLong hand on the 6 means 30 minutes

faq.q: What time should a 1st grader be able to tell?
faq.a: In Grade 1, children tell and write time to the hour and half hour on clocks with hands and on digital clocks, like 7:00 and 7:30. Telling time to 5 minutes comes in Grade 2.
Half past means 30 minutes after the hour. Half past 3 is 3:30, and the long hand points to the 6.

faq.q: Why is the hour hand between two numbers at half past?
faq.a: The hour hand moves slowly all hour. At 3:30 it is halfway from the 3 to the 4, so the hour is still 3.

faq.q: How do I teach my child to tell time to the hour?
faq.a: Start with the long hand on the 12 and say o'clock times out loud during the day, like 7 o'clock for breakfast. Then show that the short hand points to the hour.

items.q: It is 12 o'clock. Where are the two hands?
items.e: The short hand is on the 12 for the hour. The long hand is on the 12 for 0 minutes. So both hands are on the 12, one on top of the other.
The minutes are :00. It is right on the hour, so you say 9 o'clock.
The minutes are :00. It is right on the hour, so you say 11 o'clock.
4 o'clock means the hour is 4 and there are 0 minutes. Write 4:00.

items.q: At every o'clock time, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At 1:00, 2:00, 3:00 and every o'clock time, the long hand points straight up to the 12.

items.e: Half past means half of the way around the clock. The long hand points straight down to the 6.

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30 minutes.

items.q: Luis eats breakfast. When could it be?
items.e: We eat breakfast in the morning, before school: 7:00 in the morning.

items.q: School starts. When could it be?
items.e: School starts in the morning: 8:30 in the morning. At night we are asleep.

items.q: Ben eats dinner with his family. When could it be?
items.e: Dinner is in the evening: 6:00 in the evening. 6:00 in the morning is time for breakfast.

items.q: Nora goes to bed. When could it be?
items.e: We go to bed at night: 8:00 at night. 8:00 in the morning is time for school.

items.q: It is 3:00. What time will it be in 1 hour?
items.e: In 1 hour the short hand moves to the next number. 3:00 → 4:00. (3:01 is only 1 minute later.)

items.q: It is 9:00. What time will it be in half an hour?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. The long hand moves from the 12 to the 6. 9:00 → 9:30. (10:00 is 1 hour later.)

items.q: It is 2:30. What time will it be in 1 hour?
items.e: In 1 hour the hour goes up by 1. The minutes stay the same. 2:30 → 3:30.
The clock shows 10:00. In 1 hour the short hand moves to the 11. It will be 11:00.
The clock shows 5:30. In half an hour the long hand goes from the 6 up to the 12, and a new hour starts. It will be 6:00. (6:30 is 1 hour later.)
The clock shows 1:30. 30 more minutes takes the long hand back up to the 12. It will be 2:00.

items.q: Jack's soccer game starts at 4:00. It lasts 1 hour. When does it end?
items.e: 1 hour after 4:00 is 5:00.

items.q: Ava reads a book from 7:00 to 7:30. How long does she read?
items.e: From 7:00 to 7:30 the long hand goes from the 12 to the 6. That is 30 minutes, half an hour.

items.q: Noah watches a movie. It starts at 6:30. It is 1 hour long. When does it end?
items.e: 1 hour after 6:30 is 7:30. The minutes stay the same. (7:00 is only half an hour later.)

items.q: Kai's bedtime is 8:30. It is 8:00 now. How long until bedtime?
items.e: From 8:00 to 8:30 is 30 minutes. That is half an hour.
